_comment: The channel look, in one place. Appended to every episode prompt so all videos match. Change it here and the whole channel changes. This is where a trained LoRA's trigger word goes when it exists.
base: stylised 3D rendered scene in the style of a high-end historical documentary reconstruction, matte non-reflective surfaces with soft subsurface-free shading, soft flat overcast daylight from a broad white sky with no visible sun and no hard shadows, gentle ground haze separating each layer of depth, subtle tilt-shift focus falloff so the near foreground and far distance sit slightly out of focus and the midground is sharp, muted desaturated palette of slate grey, cold green and wet brown with one restrained warm accent, calm restrained composition with generous negative space, rendered in Blender Cycles with soft global illumination and light ambient occlusion, fine even film grain, 16:9

_direction.target: The reference is a rendered scene, not a photograph and not an illustration. It reads as authored — a designer depicting a real place — which is exactly what we want. 'Stylised 3D rendered scene' plus a named render engine is what pulls Flux toward that register.
_direction.why_overcast: Flat overcast light is both accurate to a July midday in Maine and the thing that stops the image reading as a dramatic movie still. No golden hour, no sun shafts, no hero lighting.
_direction.why_tilt_shift: Focus falloff is what makes a frame read as a model of an event rather than a photo of a place. It is the single strongest cue for the 'designed, not real' quality.
_direction.faces: Figures stay distant, small in frame, and anonymous — backs, silhouettes, figures at scale. This is a real death with a living family; no recognisable likeness of anyone involved is ever rendered.
_direction.no_negative_prompt: Flux is distilled and rejects negative_prompt. Everything to avoid is phrased positively above.

notes: Vary SHOT SCALE across an episode — wide establishing, mid, tight detail. Four wides in a row read as screensavers however good each one is.
Clear foreground / midground / background separation is required: it is what the depth-parallax pass in Remotion keys off to create motion.
The single warm accent ties the stills to the amber route line in the diagrams.
